Q1
```{r}
rm(list = ls())
gc()

library(lars)

data <- read.csv("bankdatatest.csv", header=FALSE)

y <- data[, 1]

x <- as.matrix(data[, -1])

fit_lasso <- lars(x, y, type = "lasso")

cv_fit <- cv.lars(x, y, type = "lasso", K = 10)

plot(cv_fit$index, cv_fit$cv, type = "l",
     xlab = "Fraction (s)",
     ylab = "CV Error")

coef_s <- predict(fit_lasso,s = 0.2,type = "coef",mode = "fraction")$coefficients

coef_s

abs_coef <- abs(coef_s)

top5_index <- order(abs_coef, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5]

top5_index
coef_s[top5_index]

colnames(x)[top5_index]
```
At s=0.2, the LASSO coefficient estimates were obtained. Most coefficients were shrunk to zero, indicating that those predictors are not important. The five most important predictors are those with the largest absolute coefficients.

Five most important predictors are:

V27, V25, V22, V21, and V11



Q2

```{r}
library(lattice)

data <- read.csv("bankdatatest.csv", header=FALSE)

y  <- data[,1]
x1 <- data[,2]
x2 <- data[,3]

levelplot(y ~ x1 * x2, xlab = "Predictor 1", ylab = "Predictor 2",main = "Levelplot of response",col.regions = heat.colors(100))
```
The x-axis represents Predictor 1 and the y-axis represents Predictor 2, while the color intensity indicates the magnitude of the response variable. Higher response values are shown in lighter colors (yellow), while lower values are shown in darker colors (red).


Q3

```{r}
rm(list = ls())
gc()

data <- read.csv("Cancer_Data.csv")

data$diagnosis <- as.factor(data$diagnosis)


set.seed(0607)

n <- nrow(data)
nt <- round(0.8 * n)
neval <- n - nt

train_index <- sample(1:n, nt)

train <- data[train_index, ]
test  <- data[-train_index, ]



train_log <- train
test_log  <- test

train_log$diagnosis <- ifelse(train_log$diagnosis == "M", 1, 0)
test_log$diagnosis  <- ifelse(test_log$diagnosis == "M", 1, 0)


fit_log <- glm(diagnosis ~ ., data = train_log, family = binomial)


phat <- predict(fit_log, newdata = test_log, type = "response")

pred <- ifelse(phat > 0.6, 1, 0)


tab <- table(Actual = test_log$diagnosis, Predicted = pred)
tab


err <- (neval - sum(diag(tab))) / neval
err
```
60 benign cases and 48 malignant cases were classified correctly, while 6 cases were misclassified. Therefore, the misclassification error of the model is 0.0526, or about 5.26%
